memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The boys grew up, and Esau became a skillful hunter, a man of the open country, while Jacob was content to stay at home among the tents. Isaac, who had a taste for wild game, loved Esau, but Rebekah loved Jacob." - Gen 25:27-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As the boys grow, we see a family quietly dividing. Esau, the outdoorsman, becomes his father's favourite; Jacob, the home-loving one, becomes his mother's. Isaac loved Esau partly because he enjoyed the wild game Esau brought home. Two parents, two favourites, one fractured family.

This is a painful and honest picture. Favouritism among parents is a seed that grows into bitter fruit. We will watch this very split tear the family apart in the chapters to come — deception, rivalry, and years of separation all trace back, in part, to these divided loyalties. The Bible does not hide the failures of its families; it shows them plainly so we can learn.

Playing favourites — whether with children, friends, or people at church — quietly wounds and divides. God's heart is different: He shows no favouritism (Acts 10:34), and He calls us to love without partiality (Jas 2:1). In a home, fair and full love for each child is a gift that guards against years of hurt.

And yet, here is grace again: even through this flawed, divided family, God still worked out His redemptive plan. He is not defeated by our dysfunction. But we do well to learn the lesson and love our people evenly and generously.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I showing favouritism that could wound or divide?
2. Where do I need to love more evenly and generously?
3. How does it comfort me that God works even through flawed families?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, guard my heart from partiality, and help me to love the people around me fairly and fully. Thank You that Your grace works even through our broken families. Amen.
